title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Friday morning, Nov 27
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 7:17 AM ET Friday, Nov 27, 2026, the morning after Thanksgiving. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). The 'USAID Files' censorship story is still the largest query (17,635 posts in 24 hours, 3.20×, down from 25,038 last evening); a new fact-check says the viral '$200 million' ad-revenue figure is a global, annual GDI estimate, not money taken from U.S. conservative outlets (What the Fact). Trump's 'fake economic numbers' GDP claim grew to 11,765 posts as its first full day rolled into the 24-hour window; AP and BEA's own release describe a routine revision on a fixed schedule. New on the Right: Trump's Thanksgiving line that only '2%' of Somalis work without aid and 'the others should be thrown out' (1,989 posts; 1,575 overnight versus 300 a night earlier). About 95% of Somalis in Minnesota are U.S. citizens, and Trump cited no source for the figure (New York Post). On the Far Left, the Fetterman–Gillibrand backlash held its overnight pace (1,704, 3.10×), and a Schumer aide's prank edit of the celebrity letter for Van Hollen became the newest anti-Schumer exhibit before Monday's vote (6,341 posts on the Van Hollen query). Holiday volume was down on almost every carried query: Abrego Garcia fell to 6,061 and Medicare for All to 9,606. One faded card (Newsom death row) was dropped and one was added. No card topic was on the U.S. trends list, which was Black Friday and football. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this morning or carried over from last evening and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. The new Somali card is tagged Right because it turns Minnesota's fraud cases into a call to remove a mostly citizen community and casts Democrats as defenders of welfare; it comes from the President himself. The GDP card casts the midterm result as the product of 'fake' government data. The Jeffries card recasts the incoming Speaker's agenda as returning deportees and a 'far-left wish list.' The USAID card casts a past Democratic administration's programs as a censorship operation. The Abrego Garcia card uses his departure to brand the Democrats who defended him. The Mamdani hotline card uses a city figure to brand the party. The Talarico, 'do not certify' and audit cards cast doubt on elections Democrats won. The Fetterman, Van Hollen and Medicare for All cards are pressure from the party's left on Democratic leaders. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Friday, Nov 27, 2026, 7:17 AM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 7:11 AM ET. Last evening's snapshot (Nov 26, 5:25 PM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. All twelve of its narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps last evening's by 10 hours (7 AM to 5 PM ET Thursday), so each card also reports its overnight count (5 PM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday) against the same hours a night earlier. Thanksgiving and Black Friday lowered volume on almost every query, so read 'cooling' with the holiday in mind. One card was dropped because it faded: Newsom death row (824 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.27× its prior daily average; last evening 1,799; 242 overnight versus 1,217 a night earlier). Its fact-check remains in the Nov. 26 snapshots. One card was added with a new query: Trump's Thanksgiving call for Somalis on public assistance to be 'thrown out.' Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: the Schumer aide's edit of the Van Hollen celebrity letter (407 posts, 0.80×; on the Van Hollen card); Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Schumer remark (509 posts, 0.26×; noted on the Medicare for All card); Jeffries' first-100-days agenda framed as a 'wish list' (192 posts, 0.77×; noted on the Jeffries card); New York politicians' calls for Puerto Rican independence, summarized by X News (233 posts, 2.15×); and 'Democrats are the party of the rich' after an income-sorting chart of House districts (55 posts, 14.35×, from a near-zero base).

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 8:00 AM ET Friday, Nov 20, through 7:00 AM ET Friday, Nov 27. The sum is the 'seven-day' total; the last 24 hours (7:00 AM ET Thursday through 7:00 AM ET Friday) are the 24-hour count; the last 14 hours give the overnight count, compared with hours 25–38 back (5 PM Wednesday to 7 AM Thursday ET). Daily bars are those hourly counts summed by UTC day. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved and cite on the card. Official pages, transcripts, archives, aggregators, Substack-style analysis pages, X News summaries and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets; this morning that includes BEA's release and revision table, Trump's Truth archive, Rational Ground and View from the Gallery. This morning we researched the new Somali card and re-researched the USAID, GDP and Van Hollen cards; the Fetterman card has a fresh post sample; the Medicare for All, Jeffries and Talarico cards add X News summaries only; the other cards carry last evening's research and outlet counts and say so. No card topic was on the U.S. trends list.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list when we pulled it. The USAID, GDP, Fetterman and Jeffries queries had small baselines before this week, so their acceleration indexes are maxed out; the GDP multiple in the hundreds means 'new,' not 'hundreds of times bigger.' The Somali query's prior average is inflated by an earlier spike, so its acceleration index is low even though it grew overnight. The volume ceiling this morning is 17,635 (the USAID query), down from 25,038 last evening, which raises every other card's volume index. Read the post counts alongside the scores.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The new Somali query requires Somali or Somalis plus Minnesota, 'thrown out,' welfare or 'public assistance,' so it catches Minnesota fraud-case coverage, fact-check replies and Somali-community pushback. The other queries are unchanged from last evening and carry the same caveats: the GDP query catches news relays, market feeds and rebuttals; the USAID query catches rebuttals; the Abrego Garcia query catches news relays and his defenders; the Jeffries query catches unrelated ICE posts and left criticism of Jeffries; the Mamdani query catches explainers and translations; the Talarico query catches 'flipped Texas blue' celebrations; the Fetterman query catches primary news; the 'do not certify' query catches rebuttals and other countries' elections; the Medicare for All query catches supporters, opponents and unrelated 'M4A' uses; the Van Hollen query catches syndicated news. Replies are included. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This morning we pulled fresh samples for the USAID, GDP, Somali and Fetterman queries; the other cards carry last evening's sentiment and say so. disinfo.caveatLead: A fact-check is not a volume score.
disinfo.caveatBody: New this morning: 'Only 2% of our Somalian population… have a job… without receiving Government Assistance… The others should be thrown out' has no stated source, and most of the people it targets cannot be 'thrown out': roughly 95% of Somalis in Minnesota are U.S. citizens, most born here, per the state demographer. Somali Minnesotans' labor-force participation (about 72% of those 16 and older in 2024) is above the state's 68%. Benefit use is high (84% received cash aid, food stamps or Medicaid in 2019–2023), so at most about 16% received none — not 2% (New York Post). 'Fake' pre-election GDP: AP reported BEA revises GDP and jobs data on a pre-set schedule 'without regard to the political calendar'; BEA's release attributes the 0.9-point revision to updated software-price and retail data, against a published average advance-to-second revision of 0.5 point. 'GDI killed $200 million in conservative ad revenue' is misleading: GDI's figure is a global, annual estimate of ad money redirected across thousands of sites it rated high-risk (What the Fact). Carried over from earlier snapshots: 'Fake economic numbers just prior to the Election' / a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' is false as stated. BEA released the Q3 revision from 3.4% to 4.3% on its previously announced schedule, not 'three weeks late'; the 0.9-point change was the largest since 2020 but tied for 16th since 1990 and smaller than a 1.2-point revision in Trump's first term (CNBC). Axios reported the claim of a 'purposeful' error was made without evidence; BEA attributed the change to updated software-price and retail-sales data. 'Jeffries will bring back the illegals Trump deported' still overstates what he said, but it has a real anchor: on PBS NewsHour on Nov. 10 he said 'Certainly' when asked about returning deported DACA recipients and called for 'remedial assistance' for people treated 'unfairly and unjustly' (his office's transcript; Fox News). That is not a plan to return all deportees, and no bill would do it. 'USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets': a review of the release found no USAID award to GDI and no sign its pilot ran (The Media Now). 'Jeffries promised to bring back the illegal aliens Trump deported' overstates an ambiguous moment. In the C-SPAN transcript of the Oct. 16 Pinecrest stop, Jeffries answered a question about returning people deported to third countries by calling for 'dramatic change' in enforcement and saying Trump's 'violent mass deportation machine does not get a dime'; the viral posts rest on a nod. We found no bill, budget or published Democratic plan to return deportees (Independence Journal; CBS Miami); the 'reparations' add-on in replies has no source. 'Gillibrand is stepping down from the DSCC' is not so: she has said she will seek another term, and the next Senate Democratic leader will name the chair after the Dec. 1 vote (The Hill; The Intercept argued she should be replaced). 'Texas is being stolen' / 'apply the 0.85 algorithm and Paxton wins' has no evidence behind it. Texas's first statewide risk-limiting audit confirmed the Senate result with measured risk below 1% (Texas Scorecard); a federal judge dismissed the Potter County GOP's hand-count suit as 'speculation layered on speculation' (court order; San Antonio Current); and Paxton conceded on election night, so the circulating 'cannot accept' statement attributed to him is fabricated (Lead Stories). 'The DSCC endorsed Fetterman' is misleading: Gillibrand said the committee would back him in the general election if he wins the primary, and she did not endorse him in a primary (NBC News; Newsweek; The Philadelphia Inquirer). 'The USAID Files prove USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets' goes beyond the documents: the most-cited item, a 2022 Global Disinformation Index concept note, is a proposal with no budget or award, and no public record shows USAID funded it (DC News Line); Newsweek said it is unclear which proposals were carried out. 'Mamdani is helping illegals evade ICE' describes a city legal-aid hotline that offers free immigration legal help; we found no rated fact-check, and the post itself does not urge anyone to evade enforcement (Townhall and LifeSiteNews quote it in full). 'Abrego Garcia is an MS-13 gang member' is not supported; fact-checkers found the claim rested on a 2019 informant's account and his clothing, and that he had no criminal conviction (PolitiFact; USA Today; Snopes, 2025). '38 million invalid voters' is not a finding of illegal votes: the figure's own source, Unite4Freedom, describes the 38 million as 'registrations flagged for further investigation – not 38 million proven illegal registrations,' and we found no official finding that any state's result is in doubt (Democracy Docket; WOWT).

narratives.title: 'Fake economic numbers just prior to the Election' — Trump's GDP claim keeps spreading overnight as AP and BEA's own release show a routine, scheduled revision
narratives.query: (GDP OR "economic numbers" OR "fake numbers" OR BEA) ("record setting" OR "RECORD SETTING" OR fake OR rigged OR purposeful OR investigate OR investigated OR investigation OR probe) (Trump OR election) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Celebratory on the Right ('causing mass hysteria among the radical left'); news relays and a minority of rebuttals note the revision was routine and made the economy look better
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 5 PM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday, the most-viewed was @EpochTimes' 'JUST IN: President Donald Trump is calling for an immediate investigation…' (18,065 views at sampling). @Johnnypatriot64's 'BREAKING: President Trump's held NOTHING BACK in a Thanksgiving post that is causing mass hysteria among the radical left… election fraud, and the Somali community' had 5,006 views, and @NathanielSami posted two versions (1,893 and 1,451 views). @MAGAPoint01 wrote 'HOLY SMOKES… the pre-midterm economic numbers were "FAKE"'. Rebuttals were small: @pandateemo88 ('Trump went after his own Commerce Department over a GDP number that makes the economy look better') and @unbiased_update ('alleged without evidence'). This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: Morning update (Nov 27): 11,765 posts in the last 24 hours (7 AM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday), 396.57 times the prior daily average of about 30 (last evening: 7,381 and 250.20×). From 5 PM ET Thursday (Thanksgiving) to 7 AM ET Friday the query matched 4,394 posts, versus 9 in the same hours a night earlier. Rising overnight. The query had almost no traffic before Thanksgiving, so its acceleration is maxed out; it is the second-largest query in this set. Overnight posts were mostly re-shares of Trump's 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' line and viral 'NOTHING BACK' recaps of his Thanksgiving post, plus news relays. The AP reported Trump called the pre-election figures 'fake' and demanded an investigation of the Commerce Department, and noted that GDP and jobs data are revised on a pre-set schedule 'without regard to the political calendar.' BEA's Nov. 25 release says real GDP was revised up 0.9 point to 4.3%, mainly from revised software-price data and Census retail data, partly offset by lower health-care services spending; BEA's revision table puts the average advance-to-second revision at 0.5 point. Last evening's card (Nov. 26, 5:25 PM ET): The query matched 7,381 posts in the last 24 hours (5 PM ET Wednesday to 5 PM ET Thursday), 250 times a near-zero prior daily average of about 30; 7,372 came from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Thursday, versus 30 in the same hours Wednesday. The busiest hour was 11 AM Thursday (1,550 posts). In a 10:45 AM ET Thanksgiving post on Truth Social, Trump wished a happy holiday 'to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated' (Trump's Truth archive). In a second post quoted by Axios he called it a 'massive, and purposeful, error' and asked, 'Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election?' The Bureau of Economic Analysis revised third-quarter growth on Nov. 25 from its 3.4% advance estimate to 4.3%. CNBC reported the update came on the bureau's previously announced schedule, was the largest since 2020 but tied for 16th since 1990, and that the 3.4% advance figure released days before Election Day had already beaten forecasts. The same post also wished Thanksgiving to the 'Radical Far Left,' those 'looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia,' and said Somalis on government assistance in Minnesota 'should be thrown out' (The Washington Times; Rolling Stone).
talkingPoints: They put out fake economic numbers right before the election to sink Republicans — then quietly fixed them after.
A 'record setting error,' three weeks late: the midterm result was built on rigged data.
The deep state at the statistics agencies picked the winner; investigate now.
The real economy is booming — Democrats won on a lie about it.
narratives.amplifiers: Trump's own Truth Social posts; @GuntherEagleman and copy-paste accounts (@shadygrooove, @Texpatriot26, @wtcrescuer911); @ThePatriotOasis, @ConstitustionX, @JB_Slear. Relayed neutrally by market feeds (@FirstSquawk, @DeItaone per @ClosingPrints) and CNBC.
narratives.whyItWorks: It hands a beaten party a no-fault explanation for the midterm wave: the voters weren't wrong, the numbers were. The revision is real and unusually large, so the claim starts from a true fact, and few people know GDP is estimated three times on a fixed calendar. It came from the President on a holiday, wrapped in a viral, joke-like 'thank you' format that spread as entertainment. And it fits a familiar pattern after Trump's firing of the BLS commissioner last year, so the base already distrusts federal statistics.
narratives.audience: The Republican base looking for an explanation of the midterm losses; election-integrity audiences already sharing 'do not certify' and audit claims; and market-watchers, who saw the post relayed by financial feeds.
narratives.counter: Stick to the calendar. BEA publishes three estimates of each quarter about a month apart; the Nov. 25 second estimate came out on the date announced in advance (CNBC; Axios). The revision was large but not a record — tied for 16th since 1990, and smaller than the 1.2-point revision in 2020 during Trump's first term. The 'fake' pre-election number was already a strong 3.4% that beat forecasts, so it could not have been a plot to make the economy look bad. And BEA sits in a Commerce Department run by Trump's own secretary, Howard Lutnick (Axios).

factChecks.claim: The pre-election GDP figure was 'fake' and its revision should be investigated.
factChecks.detail: AP reported that BEA routinely revises GDP, jobs and other data on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar. BEA's release attributes the 0.9-point upward revision mainly to revised software-price and retail-sales data; its published average advance-to-second revision is 0.5 point.

factChecks.claim: The Q3 GDP revision from 3.4% to 4.3% was a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' issued 'three weeks late.'
factChecks.detail: CNBC said Trump 'falsely deemed' the revision a mistake: it was released on BEA's previously announced schedule, was tied for 16th-largest since 1990, and was smaller than the 1.2-point revision in Q2 2020.

factChecks.claim: Pre-election GDP numbers were deliberately understated — a 'massive, and purposeful, error.'
factChecks.detail: Axios reported Trump made the allegation 'without evidence'; revisions are routine as fuller data arrive, and BEA explained this one by updated software-price and retail-sales data.

(@speech_of51859) and 'Pass the stuffing… DEMOCRATS HATE AMERICA' (@jimbotrump), and attacked DNC chair Ken Martin's response (@BalcazarMD). narratives.summary: New this morning. The query matched 1,989 posts in the last 24 hours (7 AM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday), only 0.26 times a prior daily average of about 7,797 that is swollen by an earlier spike in Minnesota fraud coverage. But it grew overnight: 1,575 posts from 5 PM ET Thursday to 7 AM ET Friday, versus 300 in the same hours a night earlier; the busiest hour was 8 PM Thursday (236 posts). In his 10:45 AM ET Thanksgiving post on Truth Social, Trump wrote: 'I want to thank the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job, and are actually willing to work, without receiving Government Assistance. These are wonderful American "citizens," and should be allowed to stay in our Country… The others should be thrown out, immediately, thereby saving the Great State of Minnesota' (Trump's Truth archive). The Hill said he made the claim without evidence. The New York Post said Trump cited no source, reported Census estimates that about 72% of Somali Minnesotans 16 and older were in the labor force ('looking for work') in 2024 versus 68% of Minnesotans overall, and cited the state demographer: 84% of the Somali diaspora in Minnesota received cash assistance, food stamps or Medicaid in 2019–2023, and roughly 95% are U.S. citizens, most born in the U.S. DNC Chair Ken Martin answered: 'In Minnesota, we pull up another chair at the Thanksgiving table. Trump apparently would rather deport the people sitting around it' (Fox News). Last evening this was a counted candidate quoted on the GDP card; it is carved out now because it grew overnight.
talkingPoints: Only 2% of Somalis work without welfare — the rest should go home.
Minnesota has no chance unless they're thrown out.
Minnesota's fraud scandals prove the community is milking taxpayers.
Democrats like Ken Martin would rather defend welfare than working Americans.
Thanksgiving is for Americans who work.
narratives.amplifiers: Trump's own Truth Social post; MAGA aggregator accounts such as @Johnnypatriot64, @NathanielSami and @maga_nation45 bundled it with the GDP line; Fox News and the New York Post framed it around welfare use and Minnesota fraud cases. Pushback came from DNC Chair Ken Martin, Somali-diaspora outlets (@VoiceofHorn, @SomaliReport_) and fact-check replies.
narratives.whyItWorks: It attaches a vivid, specific-sounding number ('2%') to a real and heavily covered set of Minnesota fraud prosecutions, so it feels like data rather than a slur. It rides a true underlying fact — high benefit use in survey data — to a false conclusion about who can be 'thrown out.' It came wrapped in a holiday message that spread as entertainment, and it lets the Right recast the Democrats' midterm win as a defense of welfare.
narratives.audience: Immigration hawks and the Republican base; Minnesota conservatives following the state's fraud cases; voters angry about welfare spending. It also mobilizes Somali Americans and Minnesota Democrats against Trump.
narratives.counter: Lead with citizenship: about 95% of Somalis in Minnesota are U.S. citizens and most were born here, so there is no one to 'throw out' (New York Post, citing the state demographer). Then the work numbers: Somali Minnesotans' labor-force participation (about 72%) is above the state's 68%. Benefit use is high and fraud cases are real and being prosecuted — say so — but neither makes the '2%' figure true, and Trump cited no source for it.

factChecks.claim: Only '2%' of the Somali population works without receiving government assistance; the rest should be 'thrown out' of the country.
factChecks.rating: No source; most are citizens (New York Post reporting)
factChecks.detail: The New York Post said Trump cited no source. It reported that about 72% of Somali Minnesotans 16 and older were in the labor force in 2024, that 84% of the Somali diaspora in Minnesota received cash aid, food stamps or Medicaid in 2019–2023 (so at most about 16% received none), and that roughly 95% are U.S. citizens, most born in the U.S.

narratives.title: 'Mamdani is teaching illegals in Arabic how to fight ICE' — the NYC mayor's multilingual hotline post becomes the Right's Thanksgiving-week case against sanctuary Democrats
narratives.query: Mamdani (hotline OR Arabic OR ICE) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Angry and mocking on the Right ('Islamist mayor,' 'Saddam Mamdani,' 'is Zohran Mamdani the mayor of New York City or…'); tied to the Jin Yu murder; a smaller set of posts translates the message and notes it is a legal-aid line
narratives.sentimentNote: We did not pull a fresh post sample for this card this morning; the sentiment label is carried over from last evening's card. Last evening's note: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Wednesday, Right posts led: 'Thanksgiving week, and New York's Islamist mayor is running a City Hall hotline seven days a week, in Arabic and English, to help people fight ICE' (@camerickson, 3,406 views) and 'MAMDANI JUST POSTED THE SAME MESSAGE 12 TIMES. IN 12 LANGUAGES… It was a hotline to help people fight ICE. NYC residents - you're paying for it' (@apinionsvary, 1,005 views). The Manhattan Institute contrasted it with the city's silence on whether the man charged with killing 62-year-old Jin Yu should have been released: 'The mayor has, however, posted the ICE hotline in 13 different languages' (@ManhattanInst, 1,216 views). Libs of TikTok's post ('Mamdani is now instructing illegals in Arabic how to fight deportation') had more than 420,000 views when Joe Pags quoted it. Other posts simply translated it: 'ICE does not take a day off from tearing New York City's families apart. We won't take a day off from fighting back' (@KimWheatley18). This is a read of that sample, not a poll.

talkingPoints: Mamdani is telling illegal aliens in Arabic how to fight ICE — on your dime.
He posted the hotline in 13 languages but can't answer for releasing the man charged with killing Jin Yu.
'Resisting' federal law enforcement is not a city service.
This is what Democratic sanctuary cities look like: taxpayer-funded lawyers for deportation cases.
Islamist mayor, Thanksgiving week, and his priority is ICE.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Libs of TikTok (per Joe Pags), @camerickson, @apinionsvary, @UHN_Breaking, the Manhattan Institute, Townhall's Amy Curtis, LifeSiteNews, Joe Pags, Next News Network (citing Breitbart and RedState), and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin on the Jin Yu case. Translators and explainers: @KimWheatley18, @MorseReport.
narratives.whyItWorks: It packs three of the Right's strongest frames into one screenshot: a Muslim socialist mayor, a foreign script, and 'resisting' ICE. The Arabic version does the work without any argument, and the Jin Yu murder gives it a victim and a villain in the same week. It also nationalizes Mamdani as the face of the incoming Democratic majority, so a city legal-aid line becomes a statement about what Democrats will do with power.
narratives.audience: The Republican base and immigration hawks; New York outer-borough voters worried about crime after the Jin Yu killing; Jewish and pro-Israel voters primed by 'Islamist' framing; and national swing voters who know Mamdani only as a symbol.
narratives.counter: Lead with what it is: a legal-aid hotline that has existed for years, in the languages New Yorkers speak. A lawyer is not an escape hatch; everyone in an immigration case is entitled to one, and immigration courts work better and faster when people have counsel. Don't dodge Jin Yu: say clearly that someone charged with murder and a prior deportation should be handed to ICE, and press for the specific detainer facts. Then call the 'Arabic' outrage what it is: a city posting in 13 languages, one of which is being used to scare people.
